title: The Brualdi–Ryser conjecture for partial transversals in latin squares
statement:
Let $L$ be a latin square of order $n$. A **near transversal** is a partial transversal of size $n-1$, and a **transversal** is a partial transversal of size $n$.

**Brualdi–Ryser conjecture.** Every latin square $L$ of order $n$ possesses a near transversal, and if $n$ is odd then $L$ possesses a transversal.

These are longstanding conjectures on the existence of large partial transversals in latin squares. The source explains that the chromatic number conjecture would imply them; their status remains open.
source_name: Luis Goddyn, Kevin Halasz and E. S. Mahmoodian, “The Chromatic Number of Finite Group Cayley Tables”, arXiv:1805.06979 (2018).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0911.4008](https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.4008).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06979

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).
